The show popped into the Seattle match and captured the Reign’s go-ahead goal, vital for their playoff hopes. A poignant moment came 14 minutes later, when Jess Fishlock subbed off and a national audience could watch the farewell of an NWSL icon.View image in fullscreenMegan Rapinoe called into ESPN’s show from Seattle, where she was watching longtime Reign teammate Jess Fishlock’s final regular-season match.Photograph: Melissa Levin/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock“When you’re in it, there’s so much pressure to be able to perform and apply everything you’ve worked towards,” said Krieger who, like Fishlock, played the final regular-season minutes of her career on a Decision Day. “There’s a different fire that comes out in players when there’s something to fight for more than just a win.”It has been a mixed time for the NWSL’s media deal, which was valued at $60m per season upon signing in 2023 and runs through the 2027 campaign. The league had to drop one partner, Victory+, because of the streamer’s missed payments, and the fragmented slate forces viewers to pay for many platforms. But there’s also been marked growth. Across four Women’s Sports Sundays telecasts on ESPN, the soccer matches averaged 255,000 viewers, up 106% against the regular-season average last year. NWSL viewership is up on all three of ESPN’s linear platforms.Of the possible scenarios, the one that played out was not the most dramatic, but it was a satisfying close. Gotham became first-time Shield winners; Kansas City and Washington ensured their home quarter-finals; Seattle clinched the final playoff spot; and Utah secured theirs for the first time in club history.Gotham’s Shield lift, with the backdrop of fireworks and their home fans at Sports Illustrated Stadium, made for an apt closing visual. (Had San Diego jumped Gotham to win, they would have received medals in San Jose, then the sterling silver trophy next week.)The crew at ESPN signed off, posed for some pictures and then turned to work on the next assignment: sorting out plans for the playoffs, which begin Friday.Explore more on these topicsNWSLUS sports mediaWomen's footballESPNUS television industryfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Marco Rose’s tactics are lifting Bournemouth, Roméo Lavia makes progress with Chelsea and Roberto De Zerbi gives youth a chance at Spurs
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Marco Rose’s tactics are lifting Bournemouth, Roméo Lavia makes progress with Chelsea and Roberto De Zerbi gives youth a chance at Spurs
Content: Aston Villa’s Unai Emery, Roméo Lavia of Chelsea and Ipswich’s Julio Enciso.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty)View image in fullscreenAston Villa’s Unai Emery, Roméo Lavia of Chelsea and Ipswich’s Julio Enciso.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Getty)Ten talking points from the weekend footballPremier LeaguePremier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionMarco Rose’s tactics are lifting Bournemouth, Roméo Lavia makes progress with Chelsea and Roberto De Zerbi gives youth a chance at SpursGuardian sportMon 2 Nov 2026 03.00 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 10.52 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Arsenal show maturity and qualityGood defending is the mark of champions. At Anfield, where Arsenal had not won in the past 13 visits, Mikel Arteta followed the orthodoxy of locking down once his team took the lead. This time around, it proved successful. Arsenal did not allow the occasion or the stadium to get to them as they have on previous occasions. In April 2023, Granit Xhaka entangling with Trent Alexander-Arnold energised home fans previously despondent that Arsenal were 2-0 up. It finished 2-2. On Sunday, Liverpool zipped around zestfully, as Andoni Iraola requests, though the final-ball quality was lacking. That owed a great deal to the organisation of the Arsenal defence. Ahead of the last international break, Brighton set a blueprint for getting the better of Arsenal inwinning 3-0. Liverpool’s squad profile might have made a similar strategy possible though Iraola’s outfit is struggling to create chances in the same volume as Brighton or his Bournemouth team.John BrewinMatch report:Liverpool 0-1 ArsenalView image in fullscreenKai Havertz scores the only goal at Anfield.Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters2Reds’ attacking flurries not enoughNo shots on target forLiverpool, leaving them with zero margin for the errors that preceded Kai Havertz’s decisive goal. Nine points behind Arsenal with a quarter of the season gone, Liverpool’s season risks becoming a developmental one, a time to regroup and rethink rather than challenging for the title. The squad Iraola inherited still bears the weight of the failed rebuild of the summer of 2025. Florian Wirtz was both unlucky when rattling the crossbar and too ponderous when a second-half chance dropped his way. Alexander Isak is nothing like the busy-bee striker his manager asks to press from the front. Milos Kerkez continues to be chaotic. Bradley Barcola, 2026’s headline signing, played his part in the flurry that followed Arsenal’s goal but faded, as did his fellow forwards. There are shards of light. Jérémy Jacquet and Trey Nyoni (aggressive – perhaps too aggressive – and involved in his hour on the field) are young players who can go places. Though it may take some time for Liverpool to get there as a team.JBReaction:Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial3Emery can keep Villa in the sunThe small matter of a glamorous trip to Barcelona comes first for Aston Villa but it is a quirk of timing that Unai Emery’s next Premier League assignment should come at Old Trafford. It is the historical stature of Manchester United thattriggered all the controversyover Jamie Carragher’s claim that Emery should be looking to climb the football chain and consider succeeding Michael Carrick should he be sacked. But even if Emery perceived United as a step up (as Youri Tielemans didwhen trading clubs in the summer, and look where that’s led him), would he prosper there? At Villa Park, he has an increasingly strong hold on how all team affairs are run, as signalled by his nominal upgrade from head coach to manager when he last signed a new contract, and he will visit the Camp Nou looking to extend Villa’s 100% start to their Champions League campaign. Having suffered dips at Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal, there is no certainty Emery’s methods would work in the febrile cauldron that is Old Trafford. After all, Manchester United will never be Aston Villa.Peter LansleyMatch report:Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham4Rose helping Bournemouth bloomBournemouth are in full flow, winning each of their past six matches, scoring 16 goals. All while Alex Scott is absent with the muscle injury sustained with England. Those goals have come unanswered. Marco Rose has added a defensive solidity not always present during Iraola’s era. Last season’s goal difference was +4. Djordje Petrovic has not conceded a goalsince the 5-1 defeatat Chelsea on 10 October. “The Chelsea game was the moment we changed all momentum,” said Petrovic after beating Leeds. Rose has admitted testing opening weeks in the Premier League had altered perceptions to force a rethink. “Everyone in the team, starting from the attackers, is doing their job offensively and defensively,” Petrovic said. Since Stamford Bridge, commitment to the collective has paid impressive dividends. “If you have that intensity with the attackers, it gets easier, we have a good group of players with quality and huge rotations in each position.”JBMatch report:Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds UnitedChart showing top teams for expected goal difference in the 2026-27 Premier League5Lavia’s potential on show at lastRoméo Lavia completed his first 90 minutes as a Chelsea player during theirCarabao Cup defeat by Liverpoollast Wednesday. It was a major milestone for a player who has struggled to stay fit since joining from Southampton three years ago. Lavia’s injury record invites caution but the midfielder is making progress. He followed up his performance against Liverpool with his second consecutive 90-minute display when Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 on Saturday. “As long as I feel good, I’ll do everything possible to help the team to get this type of result and I’m feeling good, so I’m very happy with my performance,” Lavia said after starring against United and creating the opening goal for Morgan Rogers. “All I can say is that the work that we’re doing with all the people at the club is going well. It’s just about keeping it going. Hopefully it can continue this way.”Jacob SteinbergMatch report:Chelsea 2-0 Manchester UnitedChart showing percentage of possible minutes played by Roméo Lavia for Chelsea6Rising star Williams-Barnett gets chanceWith Tottenham cruising towards athird successive Premier League victory, against 10-man Crystal Palace, Roberto De Zerbi decided the time had come in the 88th minute. Luca Williams-Barnett is rated asone of the best prospectsto emerge from the Spurs academy in many years but the attacking midfielder has had to be patient for his first league appearance as De Zerbi’s side struggled at the start of the season. The 18-year-old made an instant impression with a sensational first touch and pass after replacing Mathys Tel before setting up Mohammed Kudus for a great chance, to make it 3-0, that was spurned. We can expect to see more of him if De Zerbi gets his way. “My career is clear: when I have young, talented players, nothing changes,” he said. “I thought it was the right moment for him in the Premier League – but as a quality, he’s a big, big talent.”Ed Aaronsskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMatch report:Tottenham 2-0 Crystal Palace7Hürzeler’s ‘connections’ keep Seagulls flyingAfter Fabian Hürzeler masterminded Brighton’s fine 1-0 win atManchester Citythat lifted the Seagulls to 19 points, only two behind their hosts, the manager pointed to the culture he is building. “For me, I think it’s a lot about connection. We work in the people business. And we speak a lot about players. But for me, it’s more important to understand the person behind the player. And therefore, we try to build a lot on connection. We try to build a lot on culture. Because I think having the right values, having the right connection, the right relationship between the players helps you massively on the pitch. On the pitch, they need to rely on each other, trust each other. And you can only build this on and off the pitch. And therefore, we try to emphasise this a lot.”Jamie JacksonMatch report:Manchester City 0-1 Brighton8Igor Thiago shows signs of best formThe oddity about Brentford this season is that they’re playing well, have a very good chance of qualifying for Europe for the first time in their history, and yet there’s been a feeling that they’ve been leaving points behind. Inexplicably, victory over Nottingham Forest was their first win in five and their first clean sheet since the3-0 demolition of Chelsea six weeks ago. Perhaps the biggest issue in terms of improving on last season’s ninth-placed finish was whether Igor Thiago could match his tally of 22 goals. He’s started this campaign slowly, but got his second of the season with Brentford’s second against Forest. The finish, which looped in off Nikola Milenkovic, was fortuitous and not entirely convincing, but more significant perhaps was the way he stepped back away from the defenders, creating space for Jaidon Anthony to pick him out. That instinct will always generate chances, and the finishing will surely return.Jonathan WilsonMatch report:Brentford 2-0 Nottingham Forest9Enciso can be key in fight to surviveThe word at Ipswich is that Julio Enciso has come back to the club with an increased level of maturity after a year in Ligue 1. He occasionally sparkled at Portman Road on loan from Brighton in the second half of the doomed 2024-25 season but lacked consistency. This season he already has two goals, a pair of assists and has become Ipswich’s chief creator. Enciso is comfortably top of the club’s chances-created chart, the Paraguayan’s tally of 14 is nearly double the next names on the list – Sasa Lukic, Emersonn and Abdul Fatawu, who have eight apiece. After the Tractor Boys had managed to turn a 1-0 lead into a 2-1 deficit at Hull, Enciso’s thwack from the edge of the box earned his side a vital point. He will be required to keep producing these kinds of moments if Gary O’Neil’s side are to do what they couldn’t last time around and stay in the top flight for consecutive seasons.Tom BassamMatch report:Hull City 2-2 Ipswich TownChart showing players with most chances created for the promoted clubs10Coventry take big step at Sunderland’s expenseRégis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said post-match: “First year in Europe, you will have on average 10 less points. It’s our reality.” The reality is Sunderland have 12 points fewer than they did after nine games last season and if you extrapolate their current form over 38 games it amounts to relegation. Only Crystal Palace have conceded more goals and onlyNottingham Foresthave scored fewer. It would stun no one to learn that those three clubs make up the bottom three, but what is a surprise is that three promoted sides are all looking capable of avoiding the drop. A word for Coventry, who have responded to a chastening start to the season by winning three of their past five. Beating the teams around you is important in the fight for survival and this was a big tick in that box.TBMatch report:Coventry 3-1 SunderlandPosTeamPGDPts1Arsenal99242Man City910213Brighton917194Chelsea94165Liverpool92156Brentford97147AFC Bournemouth91128Tottenham Hotspur90129Aston Villa9-31210Hull911111Leeds911112Newcastle8-21113Ipswich9-41114Everton8-11015Fulham9-2916Coventry9-7917Man Utd9-5718Crystal Palace9-12719Nottm Forest9-6620Sunderland9-105Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueTen talking points from the weekend footballLiverpoolArsenalAston VillaFulhamBournemouthLeeds UnitedfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Arsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League champions | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Sunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last season
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Sunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last season
Content: Ezri Konsa, Declan Rice and Piero Hincapié and Mikel Arteta look set for another strong title challenge.Composite: Guardian Design, Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEzri Konsa, Declan Rice and Piero Hincapié and Mikel Arteta look set for another strong title challenge.Composite: Guardian Design, Getty ImagesSoccer DeskArsenalArsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League championsSunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last seasonSign up for our free newsletter hereJonathan WilsonMon 2 Nov 2026 10.47 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 12.23 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArsenal are three points clearat the top of the Premier League table. But given the team in second are Manchester City, who are likely to be facing at the very least amajor points deduction, perhaps more significant is that they are five clear of Brighton in third. The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass.Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all overArsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. But Arsenal got through that, reset at half-time, and navigated the second half with relative comfort. For the second league game running, they denied Liverpool a shot on target.Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionRead moreIf there is a lesson, it is that Liverpool, like Brighton, demonstrated that a very aggressive press can unsettle Arsenal. But then, a very aggressive press can unsettle anybody. InArsenal’s loss at Brighton, Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas took difficult opportunities; at Anfield Liverpool were denied what should surely have been a penalty when Jurriën Timber tugged Alexander Isak’s shirt – another bad moment for VAR, in that the no-call essentially mandated players to go down and highlight contact. Later, Alexis Mac Allister put a free header over. That was the difference, and this Arsenal team will not give opponents many chances. They are good at closing games out. Ezri Konsa in particular was outstanding on Sunday.They also have a strong bench. The policy has been to make the squad deeper rather than adding the very highest quality – which is why the links with Vinícius Júnior over the summer were so unexpected. That has frustrated some, but it has been successful. Arsenal on Sunday could bring on Myles Lewis-Skelly, Piero Hincapié, Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino to protect their lead with very little diminution of quality. But it’s not just on a man-to-man level that Liverpool’s options suffer by comparison; their changes upset the balance. They never really had control of the game once Dominik Szoboszlai had come on for Trey Nyoni.It’s been a recurring feature of this season that Arsenal turn half-time draws into full-time wins – it’s already happened seven times. Winning individual games, though, is only part of it; a deeper squad means there can be more rotation, which should help prevent fatigue as the season goes on, as well as providing additional cover when injuries do occur. That said, their depth was not sufficientto get them past Fleetwoodin the Carabao Cup last week, although they will face few games in conditions as challenging as those on the Lancashire coast.There are still three-quarters of the season to go, and Arsenal were in a similarly commanding position at this stage last season, four points clear of second-placed Bournemouth after nine games. The expectation then was for a procession that didn’t materialise and looked, amid a spring wobble, to have gone awry. Then as now the feeling was not merely that Arsenal were very good, but that none of their rivals looked especially threatening.But this season they have the memory of winning the title; the insecurity of three successive second-place finishes should be lessened. There is a resilience to them that has already brought a first win at Anfield since 2012 and a victory at Nottingham Forest after successive goalless draws at the City Ground. They’re picking up points at grounds where they’ve stumbled.Last season, City were more resilient than had been anticipated. It may be a different story this time, and not just because of the potential for a savage points deduction. After seven straight wins they have lost successive league games to Aston Villa and Brighton, but the vulnerabilities that have been exposed had been apparent earlier in the season: a high defensive line that can be exploited. Liverpool are starting to coalesce under Andoni Iraola but they haven’t clicked quite yet and are, anyway, nine points adrift. Chelsea are a point better off but still a work in progress. Brighton have probably been the best other side, but they don’t have the depth to be considered a title challenger.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSunday made clear what was already widely suspected: Arsenal are the best team in the league by some margin. It’s not just their depth, their cohesion and the wide variety of situations from which they can score goals, it’s that they now have belief and are picking up points at places where they have often failed in the past. And if they do build up a substantial lead by Easter, that could be hugely beneficial to their European challenge, which remains the one unconquered frontier.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US.Subscribe for free here.Explore more on these topicsArsenalSoccer DeskPremier LeagueUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Stumbling block: Wirtz’s and Liverpool’s costly struggles against tight defences | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Credit to Arsenal for restricting opportunities at Anfield but Iraola will need his side to learn to unpick low backlines
Author: Andrew Beasley
Headline: Credit to Arsenal for restricting opportunities at Anfield but Iraola will need his side to learn to unpick low backlines
Content: Florian Wirtz under pressure from Gabriel in Arsenal’s win at Anfield on Sunday.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersView image in fullscreenFlorian Wirtz under pressure from Gabriel in Arsenal’s win at Anfield on Sunday.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersLiverpoolAnalysisStumbling block: Wirtz’s and Liverpool’s costly struggles against tight defencesAndrew BeasleyCredit to Arsenal for restricting opportunities at Anfield but Iraola will need his side to learn to unpick low backlinesMon 2 Nov 2026 13.50 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 14.57 ESTShareLiverpool did not have a shot on target intheir 1-0 defeat by Arsenalon Sunday, according to Opta, the first time they have drawn this type of blank in a Premier League game at Anfield since records began in 2003-04. They did not find the target ina goalless drawat the Emirates Stadium this year either, though in both games they struck the woodwork. The margins tend to be fine when recording statistical outliers.If Alexis Mac Allister’s floated ball from distance into David Raya’s waiting arms had actually counted as a shot, would Andoni Iraola’s side have delivered a markedly better attacking performance? Far more concerning for the Spaniard will be that his team had 52 touches in theArsenalpenalty area (which is good) to create only one Opta‑defined big chance (which is bad). The Premier League average this season is five times more efficient; 10.3 box touches per big chance.Credit to Arsenal for restricting the quality of Liverpool’s chances despite them getting repeatedly within range of their goal. Most teams have been able to do this, though. While 12 teams have had fewer touches in opposition penalty boxes thanLiverpool, only Coventry with 11 have generated fewer big chances this season than Liverpool’s 12. Everton’s Thierno Barry alone has had 15, while Manchester City’s Erling Haaland has also had more than Liverpool with 14.Chart showing penalty box touches and big chances for teams in the 2026-27 Premier LeagueLiverpool have not had this issue in Europe. They have 12 big chances in the Champions League in just three games. As two of their opponents, Lask and Villarreal, are rated by Opta as being of lower standard than any side in the Premier League, this is little surprise. The relatively low stakes of a given match in the league- phase of the Champions League encourages those matches to be more open, too.This has not been the case in the 2026-27 Premier League for Liverpool, who have spent more time building up against low defensive blocks than any other team. This is, in part, a problem of their own making as they have conceded first in five of their eight matches. Only against Ipswich and Brighton have they held two‑goal leads, meaning opponents have rarely had compelling need to significantly loosen their defensive grip.Chart showing big chance involvement in the 2026‑27 Premier League for LiverpoolIn his first Liverpool press conference, head coach Iraola spoke of embracing the challenge set by deep-lying defences. “I prefer to face low blocks in terms of: ‘OK, we will be in control of the game, probably we will concede less chances, we will spend a lot of time in the opposition half and those are the scenarios that we have to find,’” he said. Only four teams have had more touches in the opposition half or attempted more final‑third passes than Liverpool this season, but such dominance has not led to higher value chances.This is where Florian Wirtz should be making an impression. He has the ability to unpick the tightest of backlines. Yet he has not created a big chance in the league this season. If his low total of five in his debut campaign was understandable with the problems Liverpool faced on-and-off the pitch, he trailed distantly behind Dominik Szoboszlai (14), Mohamed Salah (11) and Cody Gakpo (10). Wirtz is frequently involved in dangerous areas, as his ranking of ninth in the division for final-third passes completed will attest. His contributions have been far more geared towards ball retention and circulation rather than incision, however.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionChart showing percentage of time building up against each block in the 2026-27 Premier LeagueIraola will want Liverpool to make more productive use of their high press. Most of their big chances in the league have come via corners or open-play crosses. Bradley Barcola has had moments; he recovered possessionto go clean through on goal at Brentford, before pouncing on an opposition mistake to assist Alexander Isak against Brighton. But Liverpool have produced shots from only 16.7% of their ball recoveries in the final 40 yards of the pitch, which is below average (18.4%) and the seventh-worst rate in the Premier League. Improvement here will help significantly.Big chances account for 18.1% of shots in the Premier League this season but 59.5% of the goals. They are vitally important. Liverpool’s ambitions for Iraola’s first campaign will be severely limited unless they start fashioning them far more easily.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolArsenalFootball tacticsanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Fifa to share documents on World Cup sell-off plans with council members | Fifa | The Guardian
description: Fifa will grant its council members access to documents regarding the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme in person in Switzerland
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Fifa will grant its council members access to documents regarding the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme in person in Switzerland
Content: Gianni Infantino’s Fifa had to abandon plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino’s Fifa had to abandon plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAFifaFifa to share documents on World Cup sell-off plans with council membersViewings to take place at Fifa’s headquarters in ZurichNo direct response to Uefa’s questions on governanceNick AmesMon 2 Nov 2026 17.23 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 17.56 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFifa will grant its council members access to documents regarding the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme but has not responded directly to more than 50 questions fromUefaabout its governance and recent scandals.In a letter sent to theFifaCouncil by Mattias Grafström, the governing body’s secretary general, members were told material relating to FFE will be released for them to view in person at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich. They will be allowed only to view the documents, of which the exact nature and scope are unclear, under strict confidentiality protocols. A deadline of 16 November has been set to apply for such visits; eyebrows may be raised in some quarters about the fact this is two days before candidates for the Fifa election next year are required to declare their hand.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDazn secures exclusive deal on global streaming rights for 2029 Club World CupRead moreUefa had written to Grafström on 19 Octobergiving Fifa a fortnight to answer a series of questions about FFE, the Folarin Balogun affair, the Fifa peace prize, the organisation’s relations with Donald Trump and other major decisions that have caused controversy in the past 12 months. It had asked for all documents regarding FFE to be made accessible, saying refusal to comply with any of its demands should be “justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon”.The deadline imposed by Uefa expired on Monday night, although Fifa Council members are understood to have been told a response is being worked upon and will be shared with them. Fifa’s stance is that Uefa’s questions, posed afterGianni Infantinotold delegates at the Fifa Council meeting last month to submit questions in writing before they next convened in December, were too substantial in number for the two-week turnaround.It remains to be seen whether those Fifa Council members who travel for the document inspection will depart with the answers they require. In August Uefa made an application to four courts in the US for the release of documents pertaining to FFE, with a view to lodging a criminal complaint in Switzerland alleging financial mismanagement. Preliminary rulings are yet to be handed down and the amount of information available to view may be affected. Fifa has accused Uefa of “harassment” and “misinformation” and denied wrongdoing by Infantino.As reported last weekUefa and its allies are close to identifying a candidatewho could stand against Infantino in March, with movement possible early this month.Explore more on these topicsFifaUefaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carrick not concerned about Martínez’s attitude as United prepare for Roma visit | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick has insisted he is not concerned about Lisandro Martínez’s attitude despite the defender’s recent outburst aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy and his sending off against Chelsea
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Michael Carrick has insisted he is not concerned about Lisandro Martínez’s attitude despite the defender’s recent outburst aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy and his sending off against Chelsea
Content: Michael Carrick’s Manchester United side have failed to win any of their past nine matches.Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick’s Manchester United side have failed to win any of their past nine matches.Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesManchester UnitedCarrick not concerned about Martínez’s attitude as United prepare for Roma visitDefender expected to keep place after red card at ChelseaMartínez’s ‘commitment is not an issue’, says CarrickWill UnwinMon 2 Nov 2026 10.45 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 11.52 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick has insisted he is not concerned about Lisandro Martínez’s attitude despite the defender’s recent outburst aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy which was then followed by his recklesssending off in the defeat against Chelseaat the weekend.Martínez, who was fined forhis comments about United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, is expected to keep his place for the visit of Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday as United aim to end their worst run in 38 years, having failed to win any of their past nine matches.Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?  | Andrew BeasleyRead more“I’ve got no concerns about commitment at all,” Carrick said of the Argentina World Cup winner. “Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make a decision, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue.”Away defeats against Atlético Madrid and Como have left United’s 21st in theChampions Leagueleague phase, with it felt that Carrick needs a positive result against Roma, as well as against Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday, to keep his job. Martínez is suspended for the visit of Unai Emery’s men following his red card at Stamford Bridge.“I can’t look into the future, I don’t know what’s going to happen,” Carrick insisted. “That doesn’t change the way I feel, that’s how we’re preparing for the game tomorrow and I’m really looking forward to the game.“You might think I’m crazy with the results we’ve had and what’s going on, but I genuinely can’t wait for the game tomorrow and that’s all I’m focused on. Whatever happens is going to happen after that, in whatever direction it goes in.”United’s most recent home game was the 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth, which concluded with the players being booed by the Stretford End. “In these tough times you can’t expect the fans 100,000% of the time to be happy and cheering when we’re not putting out results,” Kobbie Mainoo said. “We owe it to them to put the results out there for them to cheer again.“I feel like our way to repay that [the manager’s support] is to also be behind the manager on the pitch and off it and fight for us and fight for us as a team.”Carrick will be without Luke Shaw, Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko for the visit of Roma, while Patrick Dorgu has returned to training but is not fit enough to take part.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickChampions LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Dazn secures exclusive deal on global streaming rights for 2029 Club World Cup | Club World Cup | The Guardian
description: Dazn has secured an exclusive option for global streaming rights for the next men’s Club World Cup in 2029 in a development that deepens its partnership with Fifa
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Dazn has secured an exclusive option for global streaming rights for the next men’s Club World Cup in 2029 in a development that deepens its partnership with Fifa
Content: Reece James, watched by Donald Trump, lifts the Club World Cup trophy at MetLife Stadium in July 2025.Photograph: Carl Recine/Fifa/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenReece James, watched by Donald Trump, lifts the Club World Cup trophy at MetLife Stadium in July 2025.Photograph: Carl Recine/Fifa/Getty ImagesClub World CupDazn secures exclusive deal on global streaming rights for 2029 Club World CupDeal deepens company’s relationship with FifaDazn paid $1bn for global rights for the 2025 tournamentExclusive byMatt HughesMon 2 Nov 2026 08.00 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 12.58 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDazn has secured an exclusive option for global streaming rights for the next men’sClub World Cupin 2029 in a development that deepens its partnership with Fifa.The Saudi Arabia-backed ­streaming company came to Fifa’s aid before the inaugural 32-team Club World Cup in the US last year byagreeing to pay $1bn (£745m)for global rights for the tournament after many ­linear broadcasters and other streamers haddeclined to bid.Apple TV had held talks withFifaover a global streaming deal for 2025, but withdrew owing to a disagreement over valuation, and Fifa’s subsequent attempt to sell the rights on a regional basis foundered.Dazn’s surprise late bid, facilitated by the purchase of a 10% stake in the company by Saudi’s Surj Sports Investment group, in effect bankrolled Fifa’s $1bn prize fund, withthe winners, Chelsea, taking home about $114m (£85m).Dazn is a loss-making business despite having more than 300 ­million registered users, with its 2025 accounts showing its operating losses increased from $772.9m to $939.8m over the previous 12 months, but appears content to continue to invest heavily in rights.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The value of its Club World Cup rights deal, or the point at which the option must be triggered, is not known but will give Fifa breathing space before the second edition ofits expanded competitionthat has been designed as a major money ­spinner but remains fraught with political problems.Planning for the 2029 tournament has proved difficult, with no decisions made on venues, format or size despite longstanding discussions between Fifa and the clubs about expanding to 48 teams, first reported by the Guardian two years ago.Club World Cup progress has been a casualty of the fallout fromGianni Infantino’s aborted World Cup sell-off proposal, which led the lobby group European Football Clubsto threaten to withdrawits support. In a letter to Fifa obtained by the Guardian, EFC also expressed “serious concern and disappointment” at the delays in paying $250m in solidarity money owed to clubs from 2025 more than a year after the first competition had concluded.Relations between EFC and Fifa are understood to have improved since the withdrawal of Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise plan, but they have yet to agree the finer details of a proposed joint venture to manage the Club World Cup’s commercial operations, which may be put on hold until after the Fifa presidential election in March.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe 2030 men’s World Cup co-host Morocco will be ­favourite to host in 2029 if Infantino is re-elected given his close relationship with King Mohammed VI.Fifa’s decision to award hosting rights to the first women’s Club World Cup to the US,revealed by the Guardian last month, has strengthened Morocco’s case because the US was in the running for 2029.A jointly-hosted tournament staged by Morocco and Spain is another possibility. Portugal, the third major 2030 co-host, is understood to have reservations about holding the event.Explore more on these topicsClub World CupFifaSports rightsSaudi Arabia and sportFootball politicsFinancesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Nuno Espírito Santo under threat at West Ham after poor start to the season | West Ham United | The Guardian
description: Nuno Espírito Santo’s future at West Ham is under threat after a disappointing start to the season
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Nuno Espírito Santo’s future at West Ham is under threat after a disappointing start to the season
Content: Nuno Espírito Santo looks on during West Ham’s 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday, the London side’s second successive lose at home.Photograph: Paul Marriott/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenNuno Espírito Santo looks on during West Ham’s 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday, the London side’s second successive lose at home.Photograph: Paul Marriott/ShutterstockWest Ham UnitedNuno Espírito Santo under threat at West Ham after poor start to the seasonFavourites for promotion sit eighth in ChampionshipKey figures at club losing patience with managerJacob SteinbergMon 2 Nov 2026 07.01 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 10.24 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNuno Espírito Santo’s future at West Ham is under threat after a disappointing start to the season. West Ham are struggling to live up to their billing asChampionshipfavourites and dropped to eighth after losing 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.West Ham are intent on an instant return to the Premier League after Nuno failed to save them from relegation last season, but the setback against West Brom put another dent in their promotion push. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after consecutive defeats at home and are four points below second placed Swansea. Nuno is expected to be given time to turn the situation around but key figures have become increasingly impatient. The manager faced unrest from supporters during the West Brom game.The initial expectation was that Nuno would be fired after taking West Ham down last season. Sources indicated that David Sullivan, the club’s largest shareholder at the time, wanted to part company with the former Nottingham Forest manager. Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire, was in Nuno’s corner and is understood to have argued for continuity.Sullivan then resigned as a joint-chair and director of West Ham tofight what he described as “false allegations” concerning his personal conduct. Kretinsky became West Ham’s biggest shareholder in September, buying a stake of 46%. The agreement saw Sullivan, who is not on the board, increase his stake from 38% to 40%.Any decision on Nuno’s future will be a collective board decision. Karim Virani, the interim CEO, and Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, will have their say. West Ham, who visit Cardiff City on Wednesday, are unhappy after a run of two wins in six games and Nuno is likely to face difficult questions if he cannot inspire an improvement before this month’s international break.View image in fullscreenDejected West Ham fans depart early from the London Stadium during their team’s defeat to West Brom at the weekend.Photograph: Martin Dalton/ShutterstockWest Hamturned to Nuno after firing Graham Potter in September 2025. The 52-year-old’s tactics and signings did not convince last season and the problems have continued since relegation. West Ham sold Crysencio Summerville and Mateus Fernandes after going down but they held on to Jarrod Bowen and Tomas Soucek. They broke the EFL transfer record when they signed Arne Engels from Celtic for £22m.The feeling within West Ham is that they have the best squad in the Championship and should be playing better. But Nuno has struggled to settle on his best 11 and various problems have emerged. West Ham have kept three clean sheets in 13 games. They have started games slowly, conceding the first goal on six occasions.Their strikers – Joel Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos – all joined under Nuno and have five league goals between them this season. Bowen is the top scorer with seven but West Ham lack a clear playing identity and have not found the right balance in midfield. The squad contains two holding midfielders but Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Alvarez are both out of favour.West Ham still hope that Nuno can lead a push up the table. There have been some positive signs, including 6-0 wins over Wrexham and Lincoln, although the latter were reduced to nine men in the first half. West Ham’s best performance of the season was their gritty 1-0 win away to Swansea, suggesting they are better when there is less pressure on them to dominate games.Explore more on these topicsWest Ham UnitedChampionshipnewsShareReuse this content

title: WSL talking points: Kang could have a problem and how long can Slegers hang on? | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Arsenal dropped points again despite dominating while Lauren James had to go off in Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Arsenal dropped points again despite dominating while Lauren James had to go off in Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton
Content: From left: Chelsea’s Lauren James, Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw and Arsenal’s Alessia Russo.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenFrom left: Chelsea’s Lauren James, Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw and Arsenal’s Alessia Russo.Composite: Getty ImagesWomen's Super LeagueWSL talking points: Kang could have a problem and how long can Slegers hang on?Arsenal dropped points again despite dominating while Lauren James had to go off in Chelsea’s 6-0 win at CharltonSuzanne Wrack,Sophie Downey,Tom Garry,Emillia HawkinsandMarcus ChristensonMon 2 Nov 2026 06.29 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 08.35 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLionesses may present Uefa with problemLondon City Lionesses may have lost 2-1 to champions Manchester City, but their performances and league position have shown their European aspirations are far from unrealistic. Aided by Arsenal’s poor start, London City are third in the WSL table and were frustrated to end the day with a six-point gap to the top two after dominating in Bromley. “It’s doubly frustrating, because I think the result was not the one we deserve,” said their coach, Eder Maestre. “Manchester City are more mature. They are more used to it. When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, maybe you have more experience.” Maestre’s team have a three-point lead over fourth-placed Tottenham and if they continue their upwards trajectory and qualify for the Champions League, Uefa will be forced to tackle the possible scenario of two Michelle Kang-owned clubs, London City and OL Lyonnes, qualifying sooner than they perhaps anticipated.Suzanne WrackMatch report: London City Lionesses 1-2 Manchester CityGunners’ groundhog dayIt was groundhog day for Arsenal against Aston Villa with the Gunners going a goal down for the fifth time this season. “We just said it feels like we’re playing the same game over and over again,” said the manager, Renée Slegers. “We go one goal down from a break and we don’t start with enough urgency.” The issue for Arsenal is that opposition teams can sense this lack of urgency. Get one chance early on, take it and then capitalise on the fact that Slegers’ side just cannot break down a low block. How Slegers, her staff and the squad arrest this malaise is the big unanswered question. Thewins against Tottenhamand Benficafelt like the seeds of a turnaround in fortunes, but they papered over cracks that will be exposed again until they make more of their dominance in the final third.SWWSL roundup: Arsenal stall against Villa despite Russo strikeChart showing how many times clubs have conceded the first goal of the game in the 2026-27 Women’s Super LeagueView image in fullscreenArsenal’s struggles continue at both ends of the pitch.Photograph: Jody Demay-Davies/SPP/ShutterstockJames injury ruins Chelsea’s perfect dayThere is significant concern over Lauren James’s fitness after she suffered another injury against Charlton. The 25-year-old was forced off the pitch after pulling up off the ball in the 35th minute. “It is difficult to say,” the Chelsea manager, Sonia Bompastor, said. “I can only say it’s her hamstring and we’ll assess her later to have more detailed information.” It is the latest fitness worry for the England international who, after being limited to just 11 and six league starts in the last two campaigns respectively, had started this season in superb form with four goals in the WSL. It was the only blemish on an otherwise enjoyable afternoon for the league leaders who ran out 6-0 winners at the Valley. Defender Nathalie Björn marked her first start after months on the sidelines with the opener. Substitute Aggie Beever-Jones ended her barren spell, scoring her first league goal since September 2025. There was also an emotional moment for the young Italian midfielder Giulia Dragoni who opened her Chelsea account after coming off the bench.Sophie DowneyWSL roundup: James injured in Chelsea’s win over CharltonSpence makes history in Spurs victoryAs she led Tottenham out at St Andrew’s, Drew Spence wrote herself into the history books. Her start against Birmingham marked her 217th in the WSL, making her the competition’s new all-time record appearance maker. It is the latest accolade of a decorated career that has seen her win five league titles, four FA Cups and two League Cups. The 34-year-old Jamaica international featured in the inaugural WSL season back in 2011 with Chelsea where she spent 14 years before switching to Spurs in 2022. She was once again at the heart of Martin Ho’s midfield as Tottenham ended their three-game losing streak with a dominant 4-1 win over Birmingham. Spurs were back to their attacking best, registering 11 of their 29 shots on target, recording 61 touches in the opposition box and having four different goalscorers. The victory moves them up to fourth in the table.SDAsseyi shines in Liverpool thrashingViviane Asseyi put on a performance Zinedine Zidane would be proud of as West Ham stormed to a dominant 4-1 victory against Liverpool. The 32-year-old scored twice for the Hammers on Sunday, the second goal a brilliant free-kick from the edge of the box which flew into the top-right corner. Asseyi told the Guardian recently thatshe grew up wanting to be likethe former France international – and that excellent strike was Zidane-esque. Her double in east London took the forward up to five goals for the season, moving her to joint fifth in the Golden Boot race. “She missed a hat-trick unfortunately but I’m very happy,” the West Ham head coach, Rita Guarino, said. “She’s an incredible player. Very happy for her, very happy in the way the team help her to make this kind of performance.”Emillia Hawkinsskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionChart showing top scorers in the 2026-27 Women’s Super LeagueEverton and Manchester United need flair in windowIs creativity a problem for both of these sides? On Saturday’s evidence, yes. Both sides looked well-drilled from a defensive standpoint but this was about as textbook a 0-0 as you could imagine, with both sides registering an expected goals (xG) of under 0.5 and – according to the WSL’s official website – neither of them having any “big chances” in the game. Everton are now the joint-second lowest goalscorers in the division – only bottom-placed Charlton have scored fewer – and Manchester United are only two goals better off themselves. The leaders Chelsea have netted three times as many league goals as Manchester United’s nine already. Perhaps both of these clubs ought to be targeting inventive players with ingenuity and flair in January, to offer them a bit more unpredictability going forward.Tom GarryMatch report: Everton 0-0 Manchester UnitedChart showing expected goals in Women’s Super League in 2026‑27View image in fullscreenAndrea Medina is challenged by Hannah Blundell in a low-quality encounter on Merseyside.Photograph: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty ImagesBrighton make it three in a row at homeThe Brighton head coach, Arturo Ruiz, praised the team’s togetherness after they came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 2-1. “It’s a team win. All the players deserve today,” he said. “I don’t think that there’s one player that was much better than the others, and that’s the best thing that a team can have.” The victory moves Brighton up to sixth and they now have three straight home wins for the first time since September 2021. “As I always say, we play for the fans, we play for our people, and the three points are for them because they always support us in the best way,” Ruiz added. Palace lost but it would be remiss not to mention Annabel Blanchard’s goal for the visitors, a superbly taken long-range effort in the 34th minute.Marcus ChristensonPosTeamPGDPts1Chelsea Women823222Man City Women812223London City Lionesses810164Tottenham Hotspur Women86135Man Utd Women8-2126Brighton & Hove Albion Women84117Arsenal Women8-1108Everton Women8-2109Aston Villa Women8-51010West Ham Women8-5911Liverpool FC Women8-1812Birmingham City Women8-7613Crystal Palace Women8-10614Charlton Women8-220Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballLondon City LionessesManchester City WomenArsenal WomenAston Villa WomenChelsea WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Curtain falls on Big Show as Glenn Maxwell retires from T20 international cricket  | Australia cricket team | The Guardian
description: Australian short-form cricket star Glenn Maxwell has retired from the international game
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Australian short-form cricket star Glenn Maxwell has retired from the international game
Content: Australia’s Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from T20 international cricket.Photograph: Sameera Peiris-ICC/ICC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAustralia’s Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from T20 international cricket.Photograph: Sameera Peiris-ICC/ICC/Getty ImagesAustralia cricket teamCurtain falls on Big Show as Glenn Maxwell retires from T20 international cricketExplosive batter calls time having amassed 2,897 runs at 28.9738-year-old will continue to play franchise cricketAustralian Associated PressMon 2 Nov 2026 17.23 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAustralian short-form cricket star Glenn Maxwell has retired from the international game. The 38-year-old had already retired from one-day international cricket in 2025 but has hung up his bat and gloves for Australia’s T20 team, as well as for his state.Australia Test captain Pat Cummins to miss upcoming England matchesRead more“Post the last one-day game for Victoria, speaking to my teammates and letting them know that was going to be my last game for the state was probably harder than I thought it was going to be – got a little choked up,” Maxwell said onThe Final Word podcast.Maxwell played with Australia at the T20 World Cup in India and Sri Lanka earlier this year and across his career played 130 T20 internationals, scoring 2,897 runs at 28.97 and with a strike rate of 154.42.He also took 51 wickets and 62 catches and posted a high score of 145 not out, which he scored against Sri Lanka in 2016.“I’m grateful for the time I was able to play for my country,” he said. “If you had offered me that career when I first walked into the Vic change rooms in 2009-ish, I would have bitten your hand off.“I’m extremely grateful to have played that much for my country and to hopefully inspire some kids who want to take the game up, to want to play differently and to be open and vulnerable and to not shy away and be themselves.“It was pretty incredible when even getting my first Test cap, well and truly before I was probably ready.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAustralia’s bizarre selection choices backfired – predictably – in South Africa. It’s time for a reality check | Geoff LemonRead more“It was pretty exciting and I’m glad they took a gamble on me and I’m glad I could, at different stages, repay the faith and be afforded the chance to play as much, for as far, as I did.”Maxwell also played seven Tests for Australia and 149 ODIs, and enjoyed an expansive and productive first class and List A career with Victoria, too. He will continue to playTwenty20franchise cricket, including for the Melbourne Stars in the upcoming Big Bash League.Explore more on these topicsAustralia cricket teamTwenty20CricketAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Alex Mitchell out of Nations Championship opener in fresh England injury blow | England rugby union team | The Guardian
description: A hamstring injury has ruled the Northampton scrum-half out of the game against Australia on Sunday, which England will follow by playing New Zealand and Japan
Author: Luke McLaughlin
Headline: A hamstring injury has ruled the Northampton scrum-half out of the game against Australia on Sunday, which England will follow by playing New Zealand and Japan
Content: Alex Mitchell is the latest England player to pick up an injury before the Nations Championship.Photograph: David Rogers/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAlex Mitchell is the latest England player to pick up an injury before the Nations Championship.Photograph: David Rogers/Getty ImagesEngland rugby union teamAlex Mitchell out of Nations Championship opener in fresh England injury blowScrum-half out of game against Australia on SundayWallabies match followed by New Zealand and JapanLuke McLaughlinMon 2 Nov 2026 14.00 ESTLast modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 15.32 ESTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Northampton scrum-half Alex Mitchell has been ruled out of England’s November opener against Australia on Sunday, with Bristol’s Harry Randall and Bath’s Ben Spencer called into the squad named by the head coach,Steve Borthwick.Mitchell, established as the first‑choice No 9 under Borthwick, damaged a hamstring inNorthampton’s Prem win against Gloucesteron Saturday and will have a scan on Tuesday to determine the extent of the injury.Borthwick urges England players to improve discipline at Nations ChampionshipRead moreArchie McParland, Mitchell’s uncapped clubmate, is also sidelined for the Wallabies match after sustaining a calf injury training with England last week, following his second call-up to the senior squad. A major scrum-half rethink is consequently needed by Borthwick before a highly significant sequence of fourNations Championshipmatches.The injury-enforced absence of Mitchell and McParland means either Randall or Spencer will be on the bench against Australia, with Leicester’s Jack van Poortvliet expected to start at No 9.While Mitchell is guaranteed to return when he recovers from injury, this week represents a priceless chance for Randall and Spencer to state their respective cases, with the World Cup less than a year away.Borthwick and his staff will consider how swapping Mitchell and McParland for Randall and Spencer may affect tactics against the Wallabies. Randall is famed for a sniping running game with Bristol while Spencer, who recently returned to action for Bath after shoulder surgery, is known for his exemplary tactical kicking.Elsewhere in the backs Gloucester’s Seb Atkinson, Exeter’s Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Fin Smith of Northampton are all named in England’s 36-man squaddespite recent injury concerns. Max Ojomoh of Bath and Saracens’ Noah Caluori drop out of the group named last week.The in-form Harlequins fly-half Marcus Smith is widely expected to push his namesake Fin for the starting No 10 jersey while George Furbank, who is also in scintillating form for Quins, is a strong candidate to start at full-back.Quick GuideEngland squadShowForwards:Fin Baxter (Harlequins), Ollie Chessum (Leicester), Arthur Clark (Gloucester), Alex Coles (Northampton), Luke Cowan-Dickie (Sale), Ben Curry (Sale), Tom Curry (Sale), Theo Dan (Saracens), Ben Earl (Saracens), Greg Fisilau (Exeter), Jamie George (Saracens), Ellis Genge (Bristol), Joe Heyes (Leicester), Maro Itoje (Saracens), Emmanuel Iyogun (Northampton), George Martin (Saracens), Asher Opoku-Fordjour (Sale), Tom Pearson (Northampton), Henry Pollock (Northampton), Will Stuart (Bath).Backs:Seb Atkinson (Gloucester), Fraser Dingwall (Northampton), Immanuel Feyi-Waboso (Exeter), George Ford (Sale), Tommy Freeman (Northampton), George Furbank (Harlequins), Will Joseph (Gloucester), Joe Marchant (Sale), Cadan Murley (Harlequins), Harry Randall (Bristol), Henry Slade (Exeter), Fin Smith (Northampton), Marcus Smith (Harlequins), Ben Spencer (Bath), Freddie Steward (Leicester), Jack van Poortvliet (Leicester).Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.There is one change to the forwards from the training squadnamed last week by Borthwick: the 21-year-old Bath hooker Kepu Tuipulotu, another uncapped player, drops out because of injury, with Theo Dan of Saracens returning.Borthwick’s squad of 20 forwards and 16 backs gathered at Pennyhill Park on Monday night, with the Prem now on a break until December. After kicking off against Australia in round four of the Nations Championship, England will meet Japan and New Zealand in rounds five and six before the finals weekend at the end of the month.“We’re looking forward to getting back to Allianz Stadium for four important Test matches against top-level opposition,” Borthwick said. “These fixtures take on added significance this autumn as they represent our final opportunity to face southern hemisphere opposition before next year’s World Cup.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Facing Australia next Sunday is an exciting challenge. They have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months, and we know the quality and experience they will bring.”England’s Nations Championship plans hit by Pepper and Van Rensburg double blowRead moreScotland have had a double injury blow of their own before the conclusion of their Nations Championship campaign, with Jamie Ritchie and Elliot Millar Mills ruled out of all four November matches.Ritchie is expected to be out for four to six weeks after the flanker sustained a suspected medial collateral ligament injury in Glasgow’s United Rugby Championship win against Lions last Friday. The prop Millar Mills picked up a knee injury during Newcastle’s Prem defeat by Saracens on Saturday.Three Edinburgh forwards – the props Ollie Blyth-Lafferty and D’Arcy Rae, and the flanker Freddy Douglas – have been called into Gregor Townsend’s squad. Scotland face New Zealand on Saturday before Tests against Australia and Japan, all at Murrayfield.Explore more on these topicsEngland rugby union teamSteve BorthwickAustralia rugby union teamNations ChampionshipRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content
